parsed.explanation: The combined regime imposes universal entry-document and facility exposures: visa/passport screening enforces an M/F binary, can trigger denial, additional evidence, confiscation, stranding, and permanent fraud ineligibility. Many jurisdictions ban facilities congruent with identity; four criminalize use via trespass, with a documented capitol arrest. Immigration and national custody abuse, including sexual abuse, forced labour, conversion-style care denial and birth-sex placement, make discovery severe. Travelers with minors face care bans, sports restrictions and school investigations. Courts, hate-crime law, and some sanctuaries mitigate, but functioning institutions often enforce hostile rules. No execution or broad criminalization of presentation keeps this above severe band.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal visa/passport screening enforces M/F binary and rejects X; document/appearance discrepancies can require additional evidence, denial, confiscation, stranding, or permanent fraud ineligibility if misrepresentation is found.
entry_documents.protection: No blanket visitor entry ban; existing X passports remain valid until expiry; litigation and legal FAQ continue; Supreme Court left some process available but restrictions are operative.
entry_documents.interaction: Border screening is first gate; refusal or secondary review can escalate to detention; later state/province facility and ID rules multiply exposure. Minor's documents and care records may reveal status.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse; national corrections uses conversion-style hair/med removal; arrests can yield birth-sex placement, e.g. 24h in men's ward.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Hate-crime statute and some court injunctions exist; consular or legal recourse is not documented as effective in federal/state custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border denial, facility refusal, or fraud review can become custody; state arrest feeds federal/immigration placement; custody can out traveler to staff and other detainees.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal bar on government-funded facilities; many state/provinces restrict bathrooms/lockers in public or some private buildings; four make use criminal trespass; state law invalidates non-birth markers for facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Some states/cities have no mapped ban; 22 plus capital district protect gender identity; two sanctuary cities; courts may intervene.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Visitor uses venues under state/local authority and federal sites; refusal can trigger trespass arrest, eviction, or police contact, especially with mismatched ID.

care_services.exposure: State/province bans minors' hormones/p blockers/surgery; bars public funds for any age and inmates, no taper; school investigations and provider penalties; adult visitor may face public-insurance/provider chill.
care_services.protection: Adult private continuity not documented; existing minors allowed if already in treatment under state law; sanctuary cities and advocacy resources limited.
care_services.interaction: Traveling family seeking HRT/emergency care can force outing, refusal, or records subpoena; care denial compounds border/document and facility risk.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism prioritizes 'radically pro-transgender' groups; executive orders target schools and teachers for preferred names/pronouns; official rhetoric treats gender identity as ideology/security threat.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy says counterterrorism is not for mere disagreement; no general criminalization of trans presentation; many orders are enjoined; independent courts partly contest.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Activists, minors, or visibly trans travelers may be subjected to scrutiny, questioning, or referral; law-enforcement hostility can worsen stops and border checks.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minor faces care ban, sports ban, school investigations, public facilities restrictions, document mismatch; guardian may be forced into outing when seeking continuity or entering school/clinic.
minors_guardians.protection: No adoption discrimination statute; city sanctuary; some existing minors allowed; national hate-crime recourse is not documented as operating for visitors.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian's search for care triggers refusal or reporting; minor's school/clinic status may draw state/federal inquiries; adult and child share facility/border exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Hostile public opinion, state nondiscrimination gaps, and facility bans create harassment/service-denial risk; police may enforce restrictions; no documented mass trans killings or militia sweeps.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime law covers some violence; 23 states cover bias; 22 plus capital protect; courts can award relief, but enforcement is uneven.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Calling police can out documents or lead detention; in restrictive jurisdictions enforcement may side against traveler; in protective jurisdictions police may mitigate street friction.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Which federal/state orders remain enjoined, how far private bans reach, officer discretion, and fraud determinations are uncertain; custody data gaps; traveler may not know local rules before crossing.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Ongoing litigation, legal FAQ, ombuds/courts, some sanctuaries; court-ordered release possible in protective jurisdictions.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Protective state/city rules do not cancel federal border/custody or hostile state care/facility regimes; unknown enforcement can escalate discovery consequences.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra's border exclusion is humiliation/denial without custody or facility criminalization. Here, federal screening can strand/deny and escalate to permanent fraud bars, state facility bans, and abusive custody, so materially lower.

0.25-C has birth-sex prison placement and brief arrests, but no national care/sports/criminalization or immigration abuse. Our immigration custody sexual abuse, minor care bans, and counterterrorism framing are more severe.

Varnalia routinely criminalizes presentation, months of beatings, capital uncertainty. Our adult visitor may face refusal/detention but not broad criminalization of presentation or capital pathway, and recourse exists, so higher.

parsed.synthesis: Documented federal entry/fraud screening, state facility bans, and custody abuse form a single traveler-facing system. Protective states, hate-crime law, and courts cannot prevent federal border denial, birth-sex placement, or care refusal. A minor intensifies exposure: public funding bans, sports restrictions, school investigations, and document mismatches make care and facilities dangerous. Street hostility is elevated but not campaign-like; severity is institutional and universal enough to sit in high risk, above lethal imprisonment anchors.
